title: CI signing stage investigation notes (staging flake + timeouts)
content:
Context
- Project: On-prem offline artifact signing (Redwood Private)
- This doc captures investigation notes for intermittent failures in the CI signing stage (mostly in staging, occasionally in release-candidate runs).
- Owner: Sahana (Build/CI). Release train owner: Connor.
- Primary risk: blocked releases or, worse, pressure to use break-glass (unsigned) inappropriately.

Quick summary / current status (as of 2026-01-06)
- Failure mode is a mix of:
  1) HSM-backed signing step timing out (intermittent)
  2) “key not found / permission denied” errors tied to ephemeral runner identity or token refresh
  3) Verification integration tests flaking due to time skew / not-yet-valid cert window
- We can reduce flake substantially by:
  - pinning runner pools + increasing timeouts with bounded retries
  - making signing step single-flight + eliminating parallel sign calls to the HSM
  - using monotonic time + enforcing time sync checks (and test harness time override)
  - caching bundle assembly outputs and only signing once for a build ID

What changed recently (suspected triggers)
- 2025-12-10: increased bundle size (SBOM pointer + chart tarballs) increased time in “assemble-offline-bundle” and pushed signing later in workflow.
- 2025-12-12: staging runners moved to mixed pool (new AMI), includes different OpenSSL/libfido versions.
- 2025-12-18: tightened RBAC for signing operator role (expected); may have exposed missing scope in CI service account.

Primary symptoms
A) Timeouts in signing stage
- Intermittent, clustered during high CI load.
- Usually: job spends 10–15m waiting on sign call, then fails.

B) Permissions / auth
- Occasional “403: not authorized to use key” or “permission denied reading key handle”.
- Often correlates with token refresh / OIDC assertion errors upstream.

C) Verification test failures (not-yet-valid)
- Integration tests that verify manifest signature fail with certificate validity window complaints.
- More frequent in air-gapped test harness and in Docker-in-Docker runs.


Failure log excerpts (sanitized)

1) Timeout / HSM queueing
[2025-12-16T18:42:11Z] step: sign_bundle
[2025-12-16T18:42:11Z] cmd: redwood-sign sign --key-alias=private-release-bundle --in=manifest.canonical.json --out=manifest.sig
[2025-12-16T18:52:12Z] WARN: sign request pending (attempt=1, elapsed=601s)
[2025-12-16T18:57:13Z] WARN: sign request pending (attempt=1, elapsed=902s)
[2025-12-16T19:02:12Z] ERROR: signing timed out after 1200s (request_id=sgn_8c2f...)
[2025-12-16T19:02:12Z] NOTE: HSM endpoint healthcheck OK; latency p95=140ms

2) Auth / key handle
[2025-12-19T03:11:09Z] step: sign_bundle
[2025-12-19T03:11:10Z] ERROR: kms: AccessDeniedException: not authorized for key alias private-release-bundle
[2025-12-19T03:11:10Z] detail: assumed_role=ci-bundle-signer-staging, oidc_sub=repo:redwood-private-installer:ref:refs/heads/release

3) Not-yet-valid in verification test (installer harness)
[2025-12-22T14:21:55Z] test: verify_signature_time_window
[2025-12-22T14:21:55Z] ERROR: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2025-12-22T14:21:55Z is before 2025-12-22T14:30:00Z
[2025-12-22T14:21:55Z] env: runner_clock_source=dind, ntp=disabled, drift=-9m


Where in pipeline this happens
- Workflow: private-offline-bundle-release.yml
  - assemble-offline-bundle (build bundle layout + generate manifest + canonicalize)
  - sign-manifest (HSM/KMS sign canonical manifest)
  - verify-bundle (installer preflight verify + tamper tests)
  - publish (upload bundle tar + manifest + signature)

Observed patterns / correlations
- Timeout failures correlate with:
  - concurrently running release branch builds (2+), each triggers sign step multiple times (per platform artifact) rather than once per bundle build.
  - HSM emulator tests running in same runner pool (staging only) consuming CPU (suspected starvation / noisy neighbor).
- AccessDenied correlates with:
  - “release/*” refs vs tags (sub claim mismatch)
  - jobs re-run from UI (different auth path)
- Not-yet-valid correlates with:
  - Docker-in-Docker runners
  - customers’ air-gapped simulation harness where NTP is explicitly disabled


Hypotheses (ranked)
H1 (high): Signing step is being executed more times than intended per build, saturating HSM service and causing pending queue -> timeout.
- Evidence: multiple sign requests with same build_id and identical manifest hash.
- Action: ensure single signing operation per build_id; reuse signature artifact.

H2 (high): Staging OIDC token / role trust policy mismatch for release branch builds.
- Evidence: failures mention oidc_sub includes ref heads/release vs tags; trust policy likely expects tags for “release”.
- Action: update trust relationship to include release branches OR change workflow to sign only on tags.

H3 (medium): Clock skew in dind environment breaks x509 validity windows.
- Evidence: runner drift reported; tests fail with not-yet-valid by ~9 minutes.
- Action: preflight check that runner clock is within tolerance; for tests, allow injected time or use signatures without tight notBefore windows (needs Security review).

H4 (medium): Staging runner AMI change introduced OpenSSL mismatch causing slower key operations or handshake retries.
- Evidence: anecdotal; no clear delta yet.
- Action: compare TLS handshake stats between old/new AMI; pin sign client container image.

H5 (low): Manifest canonicalization changes cause verify step to sometimes hash different content than sign step.
- Evidence: we have at least one mismatch but it was tied to line ending conversion during artifact upload in a separate ticket; not observed consistently here.


Data collected so far
- Request counts to signing service (staging):
  - normal: 1–2 requests / bundle build
  - failing runs: 8–20 requests / bundle build (parallel matrix)
- Runner health:
  - CPU spikes in staging runner pool during sign stage (likely from unrelated workloads)
  - dind time drift observed up to -12 minutes


Repro attempts
Attempt 1: force parallelism
- Triggered matrix builds (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) with signing inside each matrix leg.
- Result: able to reproduce timeouts 2/5 times.

Attempt 2: re-run failed job from UI
- Result: higher chance of AccessDenied vs standard push-triggered run.

Attempt 3: dind with ntp disabled
- Result: consistent not-yet-valid failures once drift > ~5 minutes.


Proposed mitigations (short-term)
1) Reduce signing calls (single-flight)
- Move signing into a dedicated job that runs once (needs manifest + build_id artifacts), then downstream jobs consume manifest.sig.
- Ensure manifest.canonical.json is identical across downstream jobs (do not re-canonicalize).
- Owner: Devon + Sahana. Target: this week.

2) Increase timeout + bounded retry with jitter
- Increase sign timeout from 1200s -> 2400s, but only with 2 retries max and exponential backoff.
- Add clear log lines and request_id capture.
- Owner: Sahana.

3) Pin signing client + isolate runner pool
- Run sign stage in a dedicated runner group (no emulator tests, minimal noisy neighbors).
- Pin container image for sign client (avoid host OpenSSL drift).
- Owner: Sahana + Sean.

4) Fix OIDC trust policy / workflow gating
- Option A: sign only on tags (release-candidate + GA tags), skip for branch builds.
- Option B: expand trust policy to allow release/* refs.
- Recommendation: A for immediate risk reduction; B after Security review.
- Owner: Connor + Hanae + Marcus.

5) Time skew guardrails
- Add early step: fail fast if clock skew > 2 minutes vs a provided reference (when internet exists) OR record local monotonic time and relax notBefore checks in test harness.
- For offline simulation: allow “--diagnostic-time-override” in tests only (do not ship default permissive behavior).
- Owner: Sean (runner health) + Ethan (installer tests).


Proposed mitigations (medium-term)
- Add metrics + alerting
  - time-to-sign, sign retries, queue depth proxy (pending > 60s), AccessDenied count, not-yet-valid count.
  - hook into signing pipeline health dashboard (Linear ENG-4874).
- Add deterministic “bundle build id” artifact and assert signature uniqueness
  - if same build_id + same manifest hash => signature must match exactly; warn if multiple signing attempts occur.
- Consider moving signing service interaction earlier (after canonicalization) and making everything else depend on signed manifest.


Flaky test tracking (manual log)
Format: date | pipeline | symptom | frequency | suspected cause | next action
- 2025-12-16 | staging | sign timeout | 2/5 | HSM saturation | single-flight signing job
- 2025-12-19 | staging | AccessDenied | 1/7 | OIDC trust mismatch | adjust trust policy / tag-only signing
- 2025-12-22 | staging | not-yet-valid | 3/6 | dind clock drift | runner time checks + test override
- 2025-12-29 | rc | sign timeout | 1/3 | parallel sign calls | ensure signing not in matrix legs


Open questions
- Do we want x509 validity windows at all for this signature envelope, or rely purely on key rotation + revocation lists? (needs ADR alignment)
- For air-gapped environments, what is the expected time source during install verification? If time is unknown, do we allow verification that ignores notBefore/notAfter? (Security/GRC input needed; likely default deny + documented break-glass)
- Should CI signing be allowed for non-release branches (feature testing) using a non-production key? Might reduce pressure on release key and keep pipeline exercised.


Next steps / owners
- [Sahana] Update workflow: signing job runs once, produces manifest.sig artifact. ETA 2026-01-08.
- [Connor] Decide: tag-only signing for release train (temporary). ETA 2026-01-07.
- [Hanae] Review/patch OIDC trust policy + role assumptions. ETA 2026-01-09.
- [Sean] Create dedicated runner group for signing stage + remove emulator workloads. ETA 2026-01-10.
- [Ethan] Adjust verification integration tests to surface time skew clearly and support diagnostic override. ETA 2026-01-13.
- [Marcus] Confirm any relaxation around time checks aligns with threat model (no silent acceptance). ETA 2026-01-14.


Notes to self (Sahana)
- Don’t “fix” flake by loosening verification; keep installer fail-closed. Use diagnostics and better runner hygiene.
- Ensure all logs capture build_id, manifest sha256, signature sha256, request_id.
- If we end up needing break-glass in CI for a release candidate, treat it like an incident + evidence trail; do not normalize it.

Appendix: minimal debug commands
- Print manifest hash:
  sha256sum manifest.canonical.json
- Verify signature locally (tooling output should include key id + trust root):
  redwood-sign verify --in manifest.canonical.json --sig manifest.sig --trust-store trust_store.json
- Show runner time + drift indicators:
  date -u; cat /proc/uptime; (if available) chronyc tracking
